content:
For years, collectors have had a fascination with Jobs memorabilia, and a new item up for grabs looks particularly appealing. It's his 8th-grade science fair project, complete with two demonstration circuits and a warning note Jobs wrote to his teacher.

It had been kept at the Jobs family property in Los Altos but is now one of over 200 lots in an Apple 50th anniversary auction…

Apple is celebrating its 50th anniversary this year, and to mark the occasion, RR Auctions is holding a two-part sale titled "Steve Jobs & the Computer Revolution: The Apple 50th Anniversary Auction." The first part, which debuted Apple's first-ever company check, went for up to $2.4 million.

Part two includes the science fair project.

The warning note essentially advised the teacher that the circuits could burn out if left running too long. At the time of writing, online bids remain under $3,000, but they're sure to climb.

Also up for auction is a fully functional early Apple 1.

And a development prototype of the original iPod.
